title: Why your cat kneads you
topic: Why do cats knead with their paws?

beats.label: kneading
lines: Your cat kneading your lap is probably a leftover from its first meals.
Kittens push their front paws, one at a time, against their mother's belly while nursing, to get her milk flowing.

beats.title: The habit stays
lines: Cats carry that baby habit into adulthood. Some even suck on blankets or clothing while they knead.

beats.title: One knead
lines: Each press is firm: toes spread, claws out, then curl as the paw lifts.
Here's the twist: the undersides of their paws hold scent glands, so kneading likely leaves their scent on you.
Kneading may also feel good, like a stretch does for us, and many cats purr while doing it.
So when the slow paw-pressing starts, get comfy: a nap often comes next.

sources.claim: Kittens knead the breast while suckling, alternating forelimbs, to stimulate milk let-down; adult kneading is presumably derived from this and some cats suck on clothing or bedding while kneading.
The cat presses firmly, spreading its toes to expose its claws, then curls its toes as it lifts the paw.
Cats have scent glands on the underside of their paws, and when they knead it is likely these pheromones are transferred to the person or object.
Kneading may stimulate the cat and make it feel good, like a human stretching; it is often a precursor to sleeping, and many cats purr while kneading.
